Accused has placed the probable evidence and elicited material facts from the mouth of DW1 to rebut or to dislodge the statutory presumption which is raised in favour of complainant.
In other words accused has placed evidence to show that, alleged debt as alleged by the complainant does not exist.
Inasmuch the initial statuary presumption attached to cheque stands rebutted by the accused and the onus shifts on the complainant to prove her case beyond reasonable doubt.

30. Complaint failed to disprove and destroy the probable, convincing defence/contention of the accused that he has given his cheques as security to get the compensation amount from KHB and she further failed to prove the fact that accused has agreed to discharge the liability.
Inasmuch the aforesaid probable defence of the accused cannot be brush aside and ignored.

If the contention of the accused is improbable and far away from the truth, complainant could have tender the document to show that she is entitled for the  18 SCCH-20  C.C.No.50050/2020 compensation amount and their right over the acquired land.
Such being the case the probable contention of the accused fortifies and probabilise his defence and it crumbles the complainant version.
Accordingly the complainant has failed to prove the shifted onus/ burden on her beyond reasonable doubt.

Complainant failed to discharge the said burden inasmuch her version cannot be accepted and alleged liability cannot be attached to the accused, that to in the absence of cogent evidence to show and substantiate the allegation made against him by the complainant.
31 . It is settled position of law that, there is no hard and fast rule or straight jacket formula for the accused to rebut the presumption.

It is sufficient if the accused is able to create a doubt in the complainant case, that itself is sufficient to shift the burden back on the complainant to prove his case independently with positive evidence and beyond reasonable doubt and complainant has failed to comply the same.

10. The following points that arise for my determination:-
 -:P O I N T S:-

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Complainant has not placed any acceptable evidence on record to consider and believe her allegation that they are having legitimate share of two acres in the land in Sy No.44/1-P of Byalayalu village.
Further more, Ex.P1 is not properly stamped and it is used for different purpose and complainant has failed to prove its due execution, contents and alleged consideration stated there in.
In other words complainant has failed to prove the said agreement is lawful or it is in accordance with law and the consideration stated therein is lawful as per sec.23 of the Indian contract act and the object of the agreement is lawful.
Accordingly the said agreement as projected by the complainant can not be accepted as law full agreement.
In R.Pramila bai Vs Bhaskar Narasimhaiah- Crl.Pet.NO.1387/2011 dt; 06.07.2018 wherein Hon'ble High court of Karnataka has categorically held that, initial  15 SCCH-20  C.C.No.50050/2020 Kumari Latha Rani S M vs Purushotham H on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149800127/
8
statutory presumption can not be raised in favour of the complainant in respect of contracts and consideration which are not lawful.
Complainant has not chosen to summon or examine the accused mother so as to fortifies her allegation nor given the acceptable reasons.
28.Complainant has failed to prove the material fact that there exist enforceable debt or liability against the accused and accused has issued his cheques to discharge the liability.
It is true that debt is any liability in cash or kind due to the creditor and would basically be recoverable.
The connotation of word "debt" is basically a liability to be liquidated.
In other words debt is also a pre-existing loan.
In other words accused has placed evidence to show that, alleged debt as alleged by the complainant does not exist.
Inasmuch the initial statuary presumption attached to cheque stands rebutted by the accused and the onus shifts on the complainant to prove her case beyond reasonable doubt.
Inasmuch the aforesaid probable defence of the accused cannot be brush aside and ignored.
If the contention of the accused is improbable and far away from the truth, complainant could have tender the document to show that she is entitled for the  18 SCCH-20  C.C.No.50050/2020 compensation amount and their right over the acquired land.
Accordingly the complainant has failed to prove the shifted onus/ burden on her beyond reasonable doubt.
Complainant failed to discharge the said burden inasmuch her version cannot be accepted and alleged liability cannot be attached to the accused, that to in the absence of cogent evidence to show and substantiate the allegation made against him by the complainant.
31 . It is settled position of law that, there is no hard and fast rule or straight jacket formula for the accused to rebut the presumption.
It is sufficient if the accused is able to create a doubt in the complainant case, that itself is sufficient to shift the burden back on the complainant to prove his case independently with positive evidence and beyond reasonable doubt and complainant has failed to comply the same.
There is no material on record to disbelieve the probable defense of the accused placed on record and up on considering the defense of the accused based on evidence, and material facts elicited from the mouth of PW1 as discussed above and it probabilise the contention/defense of the accused and it is deserve to be accepted.
The probabilities placed by the accused has the capacity to preponder over the case of the complainant, inasmuch accused has successfully rebut the presumption against him and he has successfully established the fact by placing evidence that he is not liable to pay any thing to the complainant and he has created the doubt about the existence of debt in the mind of the court, by bringing on record the probable evidence and by eliciting the material facts from the mouth of PW1 and up on considering the same, this court is of the firm conclusion that, presumption is said to have been rebutted by the accused and he is able to show the existence of alleged debt is improbable,
doubtful and illegal.
33. When the accused has established and improbabilise the existence of debt by put-frothing his probable defense and eliciting the material facts from the mouth of PW.1 which fortifies his probable defence/contention.
When accused has dislodge the initial statuary presumption against him, then the said presumption will not come to the rescue of the complainant and it is incumbent on the complaint to bring on record, independent and positive proof of existence of debt.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Accused has placed cogent and probable evidence to convince the court that, the presumed facts does not exist.
Accused has placed the probable evidence and elicited material facts from the mouth of DW1 to rebut or to dislodge the statutory presumption which is raised in favour of complainant.
30. Complaint failed to disprove and destroy the probable, convincing defence/contention of the accused that he has given his cheques as security to get the compensation amount from KHB and she further failed to prove the fact that accused has agreed to discharge the liability.
